one_line: Native per-tile CGT optimization on GPU is ~15x SLOWER than the CPU L-BFGS-B production fit (route_A) and fails the quality-match gate; native training does not yield a GPU acceleration for this workload.
reasoning: G5-A and G5-B prove native CGT coefficients CAN represent the scene and the native renderer gradients are correct — capacity and correctness are NOT the blocker.

G5-C is the first stage that measures native TRAINING speed (forward+backward+optimizer) vs the production fit path. It fails decisively on the SPEED gate alone: native_teacher 3292 ms/tile vs route_A 214 ms/tile = 0.065x (15.4x slower); time-to-quality 0.53x (also slower).

The quality gate also fails as literally written (|dPSNR|=3.93 dB > 0.15), though native_teacher actually fits the teacher field MORE tightly (81.31 vs 77.38 dB held-out) — the binding failure is speed, not quality.

native_GT (the real G5 candidate: pure recon to GT, NO derivative-matching, 1 render+1 backward/iter) is ALSO slower than route_A: 840 vs 214 ms/tile = 3.9x slower. So the failure is NOT solely the FD-Jacobian overhead; it is structural (GPU underutilization on tiny per-tile problems + Adam's slow convergence vs quasi-Newton L-BFGS-B).
Per fail-closed protocol (goal sec.1 'close the lane at the first failed gate'; sec.28 'do not rescue failed G5 with a large new change'), the lane terminates at G5-C. G5-D/G5-E are NOT_REACHED.
caveats: G5-C tests SEQUENTIAL per-tile optimization (one tile at a time on GPU), matching how route_A fits tiles. A batched all-tiles-simultaneous native optimizer could amortize kernel-launch overhead — this is HYPOTHESIS/NOT_MEASURED and is explicitly OUT of scope (would be a large new change to rescue a failed gate, prohibited by sec.28).
The result is for the room scene, rank R=4, 256-px tiles, ~1.2k gaussians/tile. Larger tiles or multi-view joint optimization might shift the GPU-utilization balance — NOT_MEASURED here.
This DROP is about the per-tile optimization STEP, not the F0 forward kernel (which already gave PASS_STRONG_GPU_TRANSLATION). F0 forward speed is a separate, still-valid result.

report_separation.OBSERVED: native_teacher 3292 ms/tile, route_A 214 ms/tile, native_GT 840 ms/tile; Amdahl backward 68% / render 26%; native_teacher PSNR 81.31 vs route_A 77.38 (teacher field), native_GT 50.06 vs GT.
report_separation.EVIDENCE: preregistered full run, room, 50 tiles, R=4, 400 iters, 3 repeats, GPU0 clean-exclusive; slice self-check max_abs=0.0; JSON parses; reproducible from g5c_controlled_optimization.py.
report_separation.INFERENCE: per-tile CGT optimization is GPU-launch-overhead-bound and optimizer-inefficient (Adam vs L-BFGS-B) at this workload size.
report_separation.HYPOTHESIS: batched/joint native optimization or CUDA-graph capture might recover GPU efficiency — untested, out of scope.
report_separation.NOT_MEASURED: batched native training; garden/bicycle native training; memory/VRAM accounting for native path.
report_separation.CONCLUSION: CGT native training does not produce a meaningful, robust GPU acceleration over the existing production fit for per-tile optimization; the lane is closed DROP_NATIVE_OPTIMIZATION.
